question.problem: Consider the function $g(x,y)=xy{e}^{x+y}+{x}^{2}y.$ What is the rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,-1)$ in the direction of the vector $v=⟨3,-4⟩?$
question.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $g(x,y)$ at the point $(1,-1)$ in the direction of $v$ is equal to the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,-1).$ 

First, we find the unit vector $u$ in the direction of $v:$

$$
\begin{aligned}‖v‖ & =\sqrt{{3}^{2}+(-4)^{2}}=\sqrt{25}=5 \\ u & =\frac{1}{5}⟨3,-4⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we find the gradient $∇\,g(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $(1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,g(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(xy{e}^{x+y}+{x}^{2}y),\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(xy{e}^{x+y}+{x}^{2}y)⟩ \\  & =⟨y{e}^{x+y}+xy{e}^{x+y}+2xy,\,x{e}^{x+y}+xy{e}^{x+y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨y(1+x){e}^{x+y}+2xy,\,x(1+y){e}^{x+y}+{x}^{2}⟩ \\ ∇\,g(1,-1) & =⟨(-1)\cdot (1+1){e}^{1-1}+2\cdot 1\cdot (-1),\,1\cdot (1-1){e}^{1-1}+{1}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-4,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the directional derivative ${g}_{u}^{′}(1,-1)$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}{g}_{u}^{′}(1,-1) & =∇\,g(1,1)\cdot u \\  & =⟨-4,1⟩\cdot ⟨\frac{3}{5},-\frac{4}{5}⟩ \\  & =\frac{(-4)\cdot 3+1\cdot (-4)}{5} \\  & =-\frac{16}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$
